statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the collection of all paths from node 0 to node n-1 in graph, with each path listed once and in arbitrary order. A sequence p is such a path when len(p) >= 1, p[0] = 0, p[len(p)-1] = n-1, every p[k] with 0 <= k < len(p) satisfies 0 <= p[k] < n, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(p)-1, p[k+1] is one of the entries of graph[p[k]]. Exactly means: (1) every element r[a] with 0 <= a < len(r) is such a path; (2) every such path p equals r[a] for some a with 0 <= a < len(r), with the same length and the same entries at every index; and (3) no two distinct indices a,b with 0 <= a < b < len(r) give equal sequences r[a] and r[b]. No condition is imposed on the order of the elements of r.
preconditions: Let n = len(graph). Assume: 2 <= n <= 15; for every i with 0 <= i < n and every entry v of graph[i], 0 <= v < n and v != i; for every i with 0 <= i < n, the entries of graph[i] are pairwise distinct; the directed graph on nodes 0,...,n-1 with an edge i -> graph[i][j] for each 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < len(graph[i]) is acyclic (equivalently, no nonempty directed cycle exists).
